conflict_resolutions.NO_ORDER_CITED_IN_CURRENT_LAW: The three current-law leads (48 CFR 2823.404-70, 48 CFR 552.238-78, 41 CFR 102-76.55) are held as snippets that name EO 13101: one is a Department of Justice acquisition rule that refers to compliance with EOs 13101 and 13693, one a definition citing the order, one a General Services Administration rule citing it as an objective. Each is an agency's own text; a cross-reference in a regulation to a revoked order does not keep the order's commands in force, and EO 13423 section 11(a)(i) revoked it in 2007 without savings. No source shows a statute or rule that keeps the order itself operating, so the provisional status no stands.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register text of Executive Order 13101 of September 14, 1998, Greening the Government Through Waste Prevention, Recycling, and Federal Acquisition (63 FR 49643); the number, date and title agree with the census register row. The text is a machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF, read in full. Inventory: the dossier inventory was corrected to the 85 scopes listed in the clause sheet: the issuing paragraph is added, scopes the dossier mislabelled or duplicated (sec302-g-2 to g-5, sec302-b-dup2, sec402-b/c/d-dup2) are renamed to the sections the text shows, the seven list items of section 302(a)(1) are merged, sections 402(d)/403(a) and 901/902 are split where one span held two sections, and page furniture and part headings are cut from span ends. Ending: the order has no term, sunset or termination-on-performance clause; each dated or timed provision is a performance, action or reporting deadline. Executive Order 13423 section 11(a)(i) revokes it by number, whole and without qualifier, so every clause except section 901 first ended on 2007-01-24; section 901 revoked EO 12873 on signing, 1998-09-14. Limitation: bodies formed under the order (Steering Committee, Task Force, Agency Environmental Executives) may have had charters of their own that no held source records; the claim concerns the order's commands. AI producer hypothesis; not certification.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Candidate earlier ends examined: (1) own terms: none, and every timed provision is a deadline, not an end; (2) amendment or supersession: a by-number search of held order texts finds the order cited only in EOs 13134, 13148 and 13149 (cross-references or borrowed definitions) and in EO 13423 (the revocation); none amends, extends or ends it before 2007-01-24; (3) the Federal Register disposition-note search lists EO 13423 as the only ending event; (4) EO 13423 is therefore the first instrument that revokes it. EO 13693 section 16(a) later revokes EO 13423 without reviving this order.","independent_command_check":"The order's commands are directed to executive agencies and officers; no independent statute or rule is shown to carry any of them forward. Statutory duties the order mentions (for example under the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act or the Emergency Planning and Community Right-to-Know Act) rest on those statutes and not on the order.","savings_check":"Savings and residual effects are recorded in the savings reason: the revocations the order performed survive, and EO 13423 carries the subject forward as a successor.","scope_check":"The clause sheet covers every scope of the order from the issuing paragraph to the last section, and each scope ends on the same instrument except section 901, which was performed on signing. Amendments to the order by later instruments: none found."}

savings.reason: Executive Order 13423 section 11(a) revokes EOs 13101, 13123, 13134 (as amended), 13148 and 13149 by number, with no savings, pending-matter, transition or effective-date wording; sections 10(a) to (c) of EO 13423 are its own implementation and no-rights provisions and section 11(b) is a stand-alone Department of Defense report. One effect of EO 13101 survives it: section 901 revoked EO 12873 on signing, and revoking a revoking order does not by itself revive the order it revoked, so EO 12873 stays revoked (accrued). EO 13423 also restates the subject as duties of its own (Steering Committee in section 4(a), Federal Environmental Executive in section 6, sustainable acquisition in section 2(d), toxic and hazardous waste reduction in section 2(e)), so the subject was carried forward by a successor order and not left to lapse. EO 13693 section 16(a) later revokes EO 13423 and contains no wording reviving EO 13101. The order created no fund, property or private right (section 902). The held eCFR leads (48 CFR 2823.404-70, 48 CFR 552.238-78, 41 CFR 102-76.55) are held only as snippets that cite the order; they are agency rules that refer to it and do not themselves continue its commands. Bounded search: EO 13423 and EO 13693 texts; by-number search of held order texts (EOs 13134, 13148, 13149 and 13423 cite EO 13101, none amends or ends it); the three machine searches.
